scenes.headline: How Karotte grades a student it does not trust
scenes.sub: An RL environment framework that keeps the answer key in the sandbox
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Daucus! Today: how one framework keeps the answer key inside the sandbox, and still grades without being fooled.

scenes.text: The answer key sits in the sandbox behind a Unix user. Before grading, the framework takes the submission into custody: every student process killed, a root-only copy graded.
scenes.say: The answer key sits in the sandbox, behind a separate user. Before grading, the framework takes the submission into custody, and only the custody copy is graded.

steps.say: The student is an ordinary user. It can write its working folder, but the answer key sits in a folder only root can open.
When it finishes, every process it owns is killed and confirmed gone, and its answer is copied somewhere only root can reach.
Only then does the judge, running as root, compare that copy with the key.

scenes.title: What custody refuses
scenes.say: The copy step is where the strange hacks die.

items.say: A link pointing at the answer key is refused, and scores zero.
A named pipe that would hang the grader is refused too.
A background process waiting to swap the answer is killed first.
And files planted in the student's tools never reach root's path.

left.title: Most frameworks
items: Tests copied in after the agent stops
Grader can run beside leftover processes
left.say: Most frameworks keep the tests out, then copy them in, sometimes beside a process the agent left running.

right.title: Karotte
items: Key stays in, behind a user
Nothing of the student runs at grading
right.say: This one keeps the key in, and makes sure nothing of the student is alive when grading starts.

steps.say: Its makers tested six frameworks with a scripted cheating agent. These are their results, and their harness is not published.

scenes.label: Xiaomi images with the fix commit still on disk

scenes.text: Karotte secures the run, not what you ship. Git history or timestamps in the student's folder are yours to clean.
scenes.mark: secures the run, not what you ship
scenes.say: The same week, a leftover git history leaked answers elsewhere. This framework secures the run, not what you ship. That part is still yours.

recap: Answer key behind a separate user
scenes.say: Key behind a user. Kill, copy, then grade. And clean the student's data yourself.
